In most large U.S. metropolitan areas, public transportation commutes are longer than driving, with typical multipliers around 1.5 to 2 times longer [d1,d7]. However, in specific corridors—such as Mexico City’s Metrobús bus rapid transit system—public transport can be faster than driving, especially in high-traffic city centers [d9]. Cities with dedicated bus lanes or well-designed rail networks may also offer faster transit than driving in congested conditions [d6,d8]. Overall, the answer depends on the city and the transit service quality; in general, driving is faster, but targeted improvements can reverse that [d1,d2,d7,d9].
